title: Building effective agents

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
notes: Session, harness and execution environment separation; vendor-specific design and model-dependent scaffolding.

title: Persistence
notes: Thread checkpoint versus cross-thread store; RAM checkpoint does not survive restart.

title: Interrupts
notes: Pause/resume and node reexecution require careful side-effect placement.

title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
notes: Caller operation identity and atomic deduplication support safe retries.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
notes: Incremental work and handover artifacts in a coding harness; no guarantee of arbitrary-duration autonomy.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
notes: Parallel research case study and token/dependency costs; no general superiority claim.

title: Don’t Build Multi-Agents
notes: Engineering argument about lost context and conflicting implicit decisions, not a controlled benchmark.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
notes: Context assembly, selective retrieval and compression; avoid universal context-degradation claims.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
notes: Position sensitivity on tested models/tasks; not proof about every current model.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
notes: Combining retrieval and generation; narrow historical architecture rather than definition of all retrieval systems.

title: Memory overview
notes: Memory scope and profiles versus collections, hot-path versus background updates.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
notes: Feedback stored in episodic text without weight updates; task-scoped experimental results.

title: Agent Skills specification
notes: SKILL.md packages and progressive loading; format is not behavioral equivalence or authorization.

title: Writing effective tools for AI agents—using AI agents
notes: Tool boundaries, descriptions and efficient responses need evaluation.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
notes: Interface design affects coding-agent performance in studied environments.

title: Function calling with the Gemini API
notes: Application executes function calls; model selects names and arguments.

title: Structured outputs
notes: Schema-constrained generation; reviewed for representation boundary, not semantic correctness.

title: MCP tools specification, revision 2025-11-25
notes: Tool discovery, input/output schema and error contracts; annotations from untrusted servers are untrusted.

title: Agent2Agent protocol specification
notes: Remote agent discovery, tasks, artifacts and authorization; mutable latest URL reviewed on verification date.

title: Not what you have signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: Untrusted retrieved data can redirect model behavior.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
notes: Evaluate utility and adversarial robustness in tool environments; benchmark-bound evidence.

title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous
notes: Filesystem/network isolation and credential proxy example; do not repeat absolute security guarantee.

title: MCP security best practices
notes: Token audience, confused deputy, scopes and session threats.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
notes: Outcome versus trace, grader trade-offs and repeated-trial metrics.

title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
notes: Final database-state grading and reliability over repeated trials.

title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
notes: Search persistence with verifiable answers; explicitly incomplete proxy for real user queries.

title: Traces
notes: Distributed traces and span relationships; adaptation to agent events is editorial synthesis.

title: Exponential Backoff And Jitter
notes: Randomized retry delay reduces synchronized contention.
